title: Wayland Embedder: Restore tablet support
body:
Depends on #120831.

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

Drawing tablets were disabled under the embedder. This means that the editor and embedded game wouldn't register tablet input.

## Additional information

It was originally disabled due to some weird issues. Turns out, those were mainly compositor bugs. 

There are basically three main classes of compositors I've found: 

 1. Some notify all instances of the same tablet seat and only reference objects of the same tablet seat between them. (Great) 

 2. Some notify all instances of the same tablet seat but mix up "child objects" between them. (Workable) 

 3. Some only notify a single instance of the same tablet seat at a time. (Broken) 

Case 1 always worked apparently, I just never tested embedded tabet support on them xD 

Case 2 dropped events because some arguments were not assigned to the receiving client. This patch includes a workaround which ensures that the `zwp_tablet_tool_v2::proximity_in` event references "a" tablet from the same seat as the tool. It's not exactly ideal but it doesn't matter as Godot doesn't distinguish tablets in the first place. 

Case 3 is broken. Working around it would require a lot of work, which I don't think is justified right now. Maybe once the embedder has better abstractions, but even then those bugs arguably hinder other legitimate use-cases (for example tablet support in libdecor) and should be fixed in the first place.

---

I did some testing on my [custom Fedora 44 live DVD](https://codeberg.org/dery/custom-fedora-kiwi-descriptions). Here are the results:


| Compositor                 | Status   | Notes |
|----------------------------|----------| --- |
| kwin (KDE)                 | Workable |
| mutter (GNOME)             | Great    |
| Niri                       | Broken   | Notifies only the first (editor) seat
| Mir (miracle)              | Broken   | Tablet input doesn't work anywhere
| Weston                     | Workable | Tablet cursor is invisible (this is a fixable bug in *our* client code that also happens in some other compositors)
| cosmic-comp (COSMIC)       | Broken   | Notifies only the first (editor) seat
| ???? (Budgie)              | Broken   | Not sure what compositor it uses by default ([magpie](https://github.com/BuddiesOfBudgie/magpie)?). Notifies only the last (game) seat. Control comes back to the editor once the game closes.
| wlroots-based compositors  | Broken   | sway, labwc, wayfire, etc. Notifies only the first tablet seat instance. Reported as bug [!4033](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wlroots/wlroots/-/work_items/4033)
| muffin (Cinnamon)          | Broken   | Straight up receives invalid object IDs? `weston-tablet` doesn't work either.
| Jay                        | Great    | "Bonus" compositor (not included in the live DVD), installed through `cargo install jay-compositor`). Cares a lot about compliance.

Yea, overall support across the table is not great but at least the "big two" (KDE, GNOME) work, with some welcome smaller implementations (Weston, Jay).

To be clear, the table above is **not** criticism for any of the implementations above: the tablet protocol is complex and needs expensive hardware to test/implement properly (that's why I'd rather not "work around" case 3 in the embedder myself). A lot of the covered compositors are also smaller, experimental, or overall less mature. Lastly, clients that bind multiple tablet seats are rare (my favourite example, libdecor, [doesn't even support tablets yet](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/91921)).

If anything, I hope that this usecase will help improve all compositors in the future.
